title: Keep it safe
content:
## What you'll get

A quick checklist to keep your users' information safe - where to store secrets, what your AI agent can see, and how to protect data before you launch.

---

## Put secrets in the Env panel, never in chat

When your app needs an API key, database password, or any secret token, add it in the **Env** panel instead of typing it into the chat.

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the Env panel">
Look for the **Env** tab in your project sidebar.
</Step>

<Step title="Add your secret">
Click **Add variable**, give it a name (like `STRIPE_KEY`), and paste the secret value. Save it.
</Step>

<Step title="Use it in code">
The agent can write code that says `process.env.STRIPE_KEY`, but it never sees the actual value - that's injected at runtime only.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="warning" title="Don't paste secrets in chat">
If you type "use API key `sk-12345…`" in the chat, that text *will* be sent to the AI provider. Always use the Env panel instead.
</Callout>

Secrets stored in Env are encrypted at rest and never logged in plain text.

---

## What the AI sees (and doesn't see)

Your agent needs context to build your app, but Emergent keeps sensitive data out of its view:

| What the agent sees | What it never sees |
|---------------------|-------------------|
| Your code files | Secret values from the Env panel |
| Database schema (table names, field types) | Actual database records (unless you paste them) |
| Environment variable *names* | Environment variable *values* |
| Your prompts and chat history | Other users' projects |

<Callout type="success" title="Your data is private by default">
Your projects, chat logs, code, and secrets are **never** shared with other users or used to train LLMs. Emergent isolates every workspace and encrypts data in transit and at rest.
</Callout>

AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) process your prompts and code to respond, but - per their enterprise terms - they do not train public models on API traffic from commercial use.

---

## Add login if users need private data

Once your app is deployed, **anyone with the URL can visit it**. If each person should only see their own orders, messages, or profile, you need user accounts and authentication.

<Tip>
See [Add login & user accounts](/add-login-user-accounts) for a step-by-step guide to adding sign-in flows and protecting private data behind login screens.
</Tip>

Without login, all data in your app is visible to anyone who finds the link - so plan access control before you share your app publicly.

---

## Pre-launch safety checklist

Before you show your app to real users, run through these quick checks:

- **Secrets in Env?** – No API keys or passwords hard-coded in source files.
- **Login tested?** – If your app has user accounts, sign in as a test user and confirm they can't see another user's data.
- **Public URL reminder** – Your deployed app is accessible to anyone with the link. If that's not what you want, add authentication or remove the app from public deployment.

<Callout type="note" title="Deployed apps are public by URL">
Emergent apps deploy to a sandboxed container with a public endpoint. Do **not** hard-code sensitive data in client-side JavaScript or HTML - use environment variables and server-side logic to protect secrets.
</Callout>

---

## If something looks wrong

If you accidentally pasted a secret in chat, open a new chat thread and add the secret properly in Env. Then rotate (change) that API key with your provider so the old one can't be used.

If you suspect a data leak or access issue, contact [support@emergent.dev](mailto:support@emergent.dev) - the team can help audit logs and lock down your workspace.
